transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-10-28 15:00 UTC | Duration: 52m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Daniel Cho (Redwood SE), Alex Reed (Redwood SE), Priya Patel (MetroFlux CTO), Liam O'Connor (Platform Eng), Jae Kim (ML Eng), Nora Vega (Security Lead)

Summary:
Sofia opened with a brief overview of Redwood's hosted/dedicated/private options and focused the call on integration patterns: SDKs, LangChain/LlamaIndex bindings, gateway/proxy approach for on-prem traffic, and observability hooks for rate limiting and per-route metrics. MetroFlux is evaluating options for a production rollout Q1 2027, must meet data residency and SOC2 controls, and wants a pilot that demonstrates latency and cost for a high-throughput ingestion use case.

Topics covered: SDK quickstart, embedding pipeline integration, adapter/proxy patterns for private deployment, VPC peering and egress constraints, quota management, per-token cost estimates, and observability (trace & token-level costs).

Transcript body:
[00:00] Sofia (AE): "Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'll kick off, uh, quick agenda — who we have and then we'll go into the integration patterns Daniel will walk through. If we run long happy to, uh, run a follow up deep dive. Priya, Liam, can you hear me okay?"
[00:06] Priya (CTO): "Yep good, hear you. Thanks Sofia. We put together some context in the invite, but mostly we're trying to understand integration effort and security tradeoffs between hosted, dedicated, private — and where SDKs and the LangChain adapters fit in."
[00:18] Daniel (SE): "Cool. I'll share my screen in a sec, but quick TL;DR: hosted is fastest to get started, dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and SLOs, private gives you VPC/on-prem control with KMS integrations. All three use the same API surface so app code changes are minimal. We'll show concrete examples for LangChain and a gateway proxy pattern that MetroFlux mentioned."
[00:34] Liam (Platform): "Two constraints: 1) data can't leave EU for some pipelines; 2) we have an existing edge proxy that currently terminates traffic and does tokenization. How invasive is Redwood's gateway pattern?"
[00:48] Alex (SE): "Good question. We typically see two patterns: sidecar vs gateway. For sidecar you run a small Redwood adapter near your app that handles auth/metrics and forwards to Redwood endpoints, which is lower latency for internal calls. Gateway is a centralized proxy that can do routing, QoS, and rate limiting. Both support LangChain / LlamaIndex libs pointing at the SDK or the proxy URL. There was a note — sometimes transcription has 'KV cash' instead of 'KV cache' — our runtime relies on KV cache management for context windows."
[01:10] Jae (ML Eng): "If we use LangChain or LlamaIndex, is there a maintained Redwood adapter? We currently use local LlamaIndex for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)."
[01:18] Daniel: "Yes — we maintain community and official connectors. For LangChain we've got a redwood chain wrapper and for LlamaIndex a connector that can point at either hosted or your private endpoint. We'll share the sample repo. Note: some of the older adapters have small API name mismatches; we'll call those out in the repo README."
[01:36] Nora (Security): "From security perspective, we need SOC2, SSO/SAML support, audit logs, and key management — KMS/HSM. Do you have examples of audit log retention and what goes in the redwood private control plane?"
[01:48] Sofia: "Yes — we have a security pack (S3 link shared in chat) with SOC2, ISO snippets, and KMS integration patterns. Private offers customer-managed KMS and you keep audit logs in your environment if you run our on-prem package; hosted still stores logs but you can opt-in for longer retention or SIEM forwarding. We'll attach docs."
[02:05] Priya: "We also need per-route cost attribution — we split costs by product team. Can we get token-level breakdowns and export to our cost analytics?"
[02:12] Daniel: "Absolutely. Redwood Console exposes token-level costs and you can pull per-token metrics via the usage API or forward to your observability backend. We also provide trace hooks and sample dashboards for Grafana/Datadog. For quotas, we support token quotas per API key and route-level rate limiting."
[02:32] Liam: "What's the experience if traffic bursts spike 10x? Does dedicated handle burst capacity or do we need to provision heavy?"
[02:39] Alex: "Dedicated offers burst capacity policies, and you can configure autoscaling thresholds. There's a tradeoff — autoscale reduces latency but increases cost if sustained. We typically recommend profiling your sequence length distribution and using batching/caching recommendations from Optimize to reduce unit cost. We'll propose a config based on your sample traffic."
[02:56] Jae: "Quick perf Q: if we're doing RAG with 1-3 short docs per call, and 512 tokens context, what latency can we expect hosted vs private on-prem?"
[03:04] Daniel: "Ballpark: hosted in our EU region ~80-120ms per token generation for that workload with efficient kernels; private depends on your infra but similar numbers if you have GPU-optimized nodes. There's variability — we'll run a benchmark with your dataset. Also, network egress adds overhead for private if using hosted model variants. We can keep model execution in-region to satisfy residency."
[03:25] Priya: "Residency is mandatory for a subset of pipelines. Could we do dedicated in-region with VPC peering?"
[03:29] Sofia: "Yes, dedicated capacity can be provisioned in specific regions and we support VPC peering or private links. For strict residency you might prefer private deployments on a customer cloud region or on-prem package."
[03:40] Nora: "About PII: do you have a documented data flow for redwood hosted? We need to show where logs live, how long they persist, and deletion controls."
[03:47] Sofia: "We'll include a data flow diagram in the pack; hosted logs are encrypted at rest, retention configurable, and we support data deletion requests and SOC2 controls. For more control use Private where logs never leave your environment."
[04:00] Liam: "Integration friction: our stack is Python microservices, many use LangChain; what's the work to switch from direct OpenAI calls to Redwood?"
[04:09] Daniel: "Minimal. Replace the endpoint or use our SDK which mirrors OpenAI-ish call patterns for completions/embeddings. For LangChain there's a wrapper. For LlamaIndex you swap the connector. We will note the few edge-cases: differences in streaming semantics and function calling semantics across models, which we document."
[04:28] Priya: "Costs — can you share sample TCO for hosted vs dedicated reserve for us?"
[04:33] Sofia: "Yes — we'll share a pricing template. Typical pattern: hosted is cheapest for low to medium throughput; dedicated gives predictable unit costs at scale; private has platform license plus infra. We'll send an example with your numbers if you share traffic."
[04:47] Jae: "Observability: we want request traces correlated with our APM — is there a tracing header we can pass?"
[04:54] Alex: "Yes, we support passing X-Trace headers and propagate request IDs. You can export spans to Jaeger/OTLP. Our console also surfaces per-route latency percentiles and token heatmaps."
[05:08] Priya: "One last technical: are there limitations with current LangChain tools or LlamaIndex when using KV cache or long-running conversations? We have long chat sessions with many turns."
[05:17] Daniel: "We recommend the KV cache management pattern — some older adapter versions had issues with cache eviction leading to repeated KV cache loads. Our runtime supports continuous batching and efficient KV cache access; we'll include best practices in the sample code. Also note some transcribed words may show 'KV cash' or 'K-M-S' confusion in the notes, but docs clarify."
[05:40] Nora: "From compliance: do you have subprocessor list and data residency SLA?"
[05:46] Sofia: "Yes — included in pack. For private on-prem, you avoid subprocessors. For dedicated/hosted we'll share subprocessors and can discuss contractual SLAs."
[05:58] Priya: "Okay sounds good. Proposed pilot: 4-week pilot, run in EU region with a LangChain RAG flow against a subset of data, measure latency and cost, then decide between dedicated vs private for production. Thoughts?"
[06:12] Daniel: "Totally reasonable. For the pilot we'll do: share sample repo, run a small benchmark, set up a dedicated pilot or private eval depending on residency. We'll need infra details and traffic shape."
[06:25] Sofia: "Recap of next steps: I'll send security pack and pricing template; Priya will send infra diagram and traffic profile; Daniel will share the LangChain sample repo and propose slots for deep dive. We'll follow up with a timeboxed pilot plan."
[06:40] Priya: "Great thanks all. One note — we'll also evaluate Anthropic and Vertex for a subset; we'll keep you posted."
[06:49] Sofia: "Understood — happy to support a benchmark with those vendors too if you want an apples-to-apples."
[06:55] Liam: "Thanks, that's it from us."
[06:58] Sofia: "Thanks everyone, we'll be in touch."

End of recording.
